analysis.title: Monthly Strategy Snapshot (November 2026)
key_insights: The S&P 500 fell 0.9% in October as AI demand and financing concerns drove a Tech sell-off (-6.8% MoM). The equal weight S&P 500 outperformed the cap-weighted index by 5.9%, the widest margin since April 2009.

Q3 earnings: with nearly two-thirds of the S&P 500 reported, 81% have beaten estimates (Energy 100% beat rate). 3Q26 EPS growth is tracking ~30% YoY, the third straight quarter of 25%+ growth. Excluding Tech, EPS is growing 20% YoY.

Tech EPS is growing ~65% YoY and consensus has Tech FCF rising 52% in 2026 and 46% in 2027, ahead of the rest of the S&P 500. After the pullback, Tech trades at a 4% NTM P/E premium to the S&P 500, the narrowest since 2020.

Raymond James targets the S&P 500 at 8,450 over 12 months ($385 EPS, ~22x P/E). Preferred sectors are Tech, Industrials and Consumer Discretionary. It favors US equities, EM Asia and Japan, and is less constructive on Europe and EM LatAm.

Brazilian stocks fell 12% MoM after a surprise presidential election outcome, pulling EM LatAm down 7.6% (Brazil is 59% of the index). MSCI Europe ex-UK was down 0.2% and outperformed the S&P 500 by 1.1%, though the S&P 500 leads by 5.8% YTD.

The Fed held at 3.75%-4.00% with two voting members dissenting in favor of a 25 bp hike. The statement upgraded growth from 'solid' to 'strong'. Chair Warsh said financial conditions have tightened but are not yet restrictive. Raymond James expects one more hike in December, then a long pause.

The 10-year Treasury yield fell 35 bps in October to 4.94%, the sharpest monthly decline since February 2025, after an intra-day peak of 5.37%. The Bloomberg Treasury Index gained 2.4%. The 12-month 10-year target is 4.50%-4.75%.

IG credit returned 2.2% MoM despite spreads widening 10 bps to 90 bps, led by Tech and AI-related issuers. HY returned +0.3% MoM. CCC spreads widened to 1,116 bps, just short of the 2022 peak. Raymond James favors Treasuries, short-duration corporates and longer-dated munis over HY.
Munis rebounded 3.9% in October after their worst month since 2008 (-4.4% in September). The 10-year AAA muni-to-Treasury ratio fell below 70% from above 80%.

September CPI beat consensus: headline +0.6% MoM (3.7% YoY), core +0.3% MoM (2.6% YoY). Gasoline drove about half of the headline rise, and shelter, services, transportation and medical care also rose.
Labor data is firm. Initial claims fell to 194k and the 4-week average (~197k) is the lowest since 1969. Raymond James expects payrolls averaging ~70k/month and unemployment near 4.2% through 2027.
Housing is weak. The 30-year mortgage rate is near a three-year high of 7.24%, the NAHB index is at its lowest since June 2012 (a 14-year low), and 43% of builders are cutting prices.

WTI rose ~15% in October to ~$104/bbl, a fourth straight monthly gain and ~50% above the early-July low. Constraints on Persian Gulf exports and the risk of renewed US-Iran hostilities after the midterms support prices. The 2027 WTI target is $65 on demand destruction and supply recovery.

Gold fell 6.9% and silver 18.6% in October. Gold closed below $4,000/oz for the first time since July. Silver is down nearly 60% from its January record near $115/oz. Higher global yields are a headwind for precious metals, while industrial metals are supported by AI buildout, electrification and defense demand.

The dollar rose 0.4% MoM to its highest since March 2025, helped by a 1.7% euro decline on French political and fiscal concerns. Raymond James sees limited further upside and expects EUR/USD between 1.10 and 1.20.
China Q3 GDP grew 4.5% YoY, above expectations. Euro zone flash composite PMI fell to 51.9 as French services slipped below 50.

Seasonality: since 1950 November and December are the S&P 500's strongest two-month stretch, averaging a 3% gain and finishing higher 77% of the time, nearly 4% in midterm years. Fifth-year bull markets and the 12 months after midterms have typically been positive.

Volatility is expected to be higher. Cited catalysts include international elections, US debt-ceiling talks, global fiscal concerns, AI capex and financing uncertainty, optimistic consensus earnings, the US-Iran conflict, Russia-Ukraine and major tech IPOs.

sector_views.rationale: Strong earnings and historically moderate valuations. Tech EPS is growing ~65% YoY and the NTM P/E premium to the S&P 500 has narrowed to 4%.
AI infrastructure buildout, power generation and defense spending.
Steady job gains and income growth should help it recover from this year's underperformance.

Raymond James S&P 500 forecast: $385 EPS (forecast) at ~22x P/E for an 8,450 target over 12 months.

Fed hawkishness, including two dissents for a hike, and Treasury yields near multi-decade highs.
Renewed US-Iran hostilities after the midterms, and Persian Gulf shipping attacks.

HY credit vulnerability, with CCC spreads near their 2022 peak.
US debt-ceiling negotiations and major tech IPOs.

vol_and_positioning: Raymond James expects volatility to be higher, with bouts becoming more frequent as the economic cycle and bull market mature.

Cited volatility catalysts: international elections, US debt-ceiling negotiations, global fiscal concerns, AI capex and financing uncertainty, optimistic consensus earnings, the US-Iran conflict, Russia-Ukraine, and major tech IPOs.
The S&P 500 Equal Weight Index beat the cap-weighted index by 5.9% in October, the widest margin since April 2009.
HY is seen as more vulnerable to rising volatility. CCC spreads are 1,116 bps, just short of the 2022 peak.
geopolitical: US-Iran conflict: periodic Iranian attacks on Persian Gulf shipping keep export volumes constrained, and hostilities could resume after the US midterms. A durable deal is needed for Gulf exports to recover.
Strait of Hormuz had a brief reopening in early July, when WTI bottomed.
French political unrest, strikes and fiscal concerns weighed on the euro and French services activity.
Brazil's surprise presidential election outcome drove a 12% monthly fall in Brazilian stocks.
Russia-Ukraine war cited as a possible source of market turbulence.

tension_points.bull_case: Tech EPS is growing ~65% YoY, consensus has Tech FCF up 52% in 2026 and 46% in 2027, and Tech trades at only a 4% NTM P/E premium to the S&P 500.
tension_points.bear_case: Concerns over AI demand and financing drove a 6.8% Tech decline in October, and investors are questioning the durability of the AI buildout.

tension_points.bull_case: Moderating inflation and less Fed tightening than markets expect should pull the 10-year yield toward 4.50%-4.75%.
tension_points.bear_case: Two FOMC dissents favored a hike, September CPI beat expectations with pressure beyond energy, and Chair Warsh left the door open to further hikes.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A sustained 10-year move above 5% would likely require renewed inflation, stronger than expected growth, or a prolonged hiking cycle.

theme_stances.key_argument: Despite the October sell-off, strong earnings and moderate valuations support Tech, and the S&P 500 target rests on robust earnings growth.
theme_stances.evidence: Tech, Industrials, and Consumer Discretionary are our preferred sectors.

theme_stances.key_argument: The Fed is set to deliver one more hike in 2026 and then hold, with room to be patient as inflation cools.
theme_stances.evidence: The Fed is set to deliver one more hike in 2026 and then hold policy steady.

theme_stances.key_argument: Without a durable US-Iran deal, Gulf exports will not fully recover and prices stay well above pre-war levels, before demand destruction pulls WTI toward $65.
theme_stances.evidence: Without a durable US-Iran deal, Persian Gulf oil exports are unlikely to fully recover
